title: SEAD · mission sequence
subtitle: 2024 TTX · phased counter-SAG SEAD concept over notional 24 hours
description: Mitchell Institute SEAD team's four-phase tabletop concept: continuous ISR, stimulation/decoy/electronic attack, maritime surface-action-group strikes, and follow-on harassment/BDA (Figure 9, pp. 20–21).
assumptions: Figure 9 depicts a 24-hour conceptual cycle, but gives no exact georeferenced flight paths, target coordinates or detailed per-phase clock schedule.

The report's Figure 9 includes CCA-10/CCA-11, EA-37B and RC-135 ISR; the source text specifically identifies three CCA-10/EA-37B orbits and one RC-135 orbit. Presentation counts are not claimed to represent actual sorties.
CCA-12 was a SEAD team variant adapted from notional CCA-8; its requested quantity is not a fielded inventory.
Timeline seconds are compressed presentation time, not clock hours, and map routes are editorial illustrations.

phases.title: Phase 1 · Persistent ISR
phases.narrative: The SEAD concept begins with three continuous CCA/EA-37B ISR-support orbits and a single RC-135 Rivet Joint orbit.

phases.title: Phase 2 · Stimulate, decoy, jam
phases.narrative: The team proposed expendable CCA-9, CCA-11 and modified CCA-12 to prompt emissions and disrupt SAG air defenses.

phases.title: Phase 3 · Counter-SAG strike
phases.narrative: Notional CCA-4, CCA-7 and crewed aircraft support maritime SAG attacks with AARGM, LRASM and SiAW.

phases.title: Phase 4 · Harass and electronic attack
phases.narrative: Repeated CCA-9, CCA-11 and CCA-12 waves impose pressure between larger strikes.

phases.title: Phase 4a · Harass and assess
phases.narrative: Follow-on CCA activity performs continuing harassment and battle-damage assessment in the team's plan.
